summary: Shoppers at Amazon Fresh cashierless stores reported that the store's camera system failed to register items they took, such as several bags picked up at once. Amazon later moved away from the technology.
technical_summary: Amazon's Just Walk Out used cameras and sensors to track items shoppers took. Edge cases such as grabbing multiple identical items at once were missed, and many sales reportedly needed human video reviewers to correct assignments, which Amazon disputes.

summary: Toronto used an AI model to predict beach water quality at two beaches. A water advocacy group and later analysis found it often marked contaminated water as safe, so beaches stayed open on unsafe days.
technical_summary: Toronto Public Health used a vendor's predictive model to forecast beach water quality instead of next-day lab tests. It missed most unsafe days, and the city reportedly did not check the deployed model's performance during the summer.

summary: Amazon sellers listed products, such as furniture and religious texts, with names and descriptions that were copied chatbot refusal messages. The listings showed that no one had reviewed AI-written text before publishing.
technical_summary: Third-party sellers used a large language model to generate product titles and descriptions and pasted outputs, including refusal messages citing OpenAI's use policy, directly into listings. No human review or platform check caught the error text before publication.

sector.quote: Amazon has been hit with a wave of odd AI-generated listings

notes: Harm is mainly degraded listing quality and trust; no specific victim is described.

summary: A city traffic camera in Ningbo, China, wrongly labeled a famous businesswoman as a jaywalker because her face appeared in an advertisement on a passing bus. Police apologized and deleted the record.
technical_summary: Ningbo police used facial recognition on intersection cameras to identify jaywalkers and display them on a public screen. The system matched a face printed on a moving bus advertisement to a real person, reportedly because it lacked live-person detection.

summary: Google Translate was shown to turn gender-neutral words into gendered English sentences along stereotypes, such as translating a neutral pronoun as 'he' for engineers and 'she' for nurses.
technical_summary: Google Translate's statistical model learns patterns from large web text, so it reproduces occupational gender stereotypes when choosing a pronoun for gender-neutral source languages such as Turkish and Finnish. Word-embedding research shows such biases exist in the underlying language data.

summary: The UK government's online passport photo checker rejected photos of darker-skinned women more often than those of lighter-skinned men, according to a BBC investigation, forcing some applicants to challenge the result.
technical_summary: The passport website's automated photo-quality check was less accurate for darker skin tones. BBC tests of over 1,000 politicians' photos found darker-skinned women were rejected as poor quality more often than lighter-skinned people, sometimes for wrongly detected open mouths.

summary: The New York Police Department ended its lease of a Boston Dynamics robotic dog early after public backlash. Critics described it as a symbol of surveillance and overly aggressive policing in poor communities.

Its use at a home invasion response and a public housing building prompted criticism, and the department terminated the contract before it expired. The dispute concerned policing policy rather than a malfunction.
